parsed_allowlist.before:
Comparison purpose: keep the note pattern fixed while only the Decay envelope changes. This recipe has two exercises: compare longer and shorter Decay tails with relative turns, then try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. Use a separate project so neither changes your course arrangement.

Starting point: use an empty project at 90 BPM, Rate /1 and playback stopped. Make sure n.b. PolyPerc is installed and enabled using [Sound Sources with n.b.](#norns-sound-sources-with-n-b); assign Polyperc 1 to channel 1 with range 1–16. In Masks set default velocity 70 and Len ½. Add trig masks on odd steps by holding K1, tapping each odd step and releasing K1. Select Note with E2; for each odd step, hold it and turn E3 to set the absolute MIDI note: step 1=48, 3=55, 5=52, 7=55, 9=48, 11=55, 13=53 and 15=55. Press Channel at (3,8), select channel 1 on row 1, then tap Pattern 1 in the second-from-top grid row to assign it before playing; an empty project has no pattern assigned by default.

Controls and step map: press Channel at (3,8), select its number on row 1, then turn E1 to Channel tasks. Use E2 to highlight Device, Masks, Clock, Trig params or Harmony and K3 to open it. On Device use E2 for the row, E3 for the named sound and K3 to apply. On Masks, E2 selects Note, Vel, Len or Chd1/Chd2; E3 changes the value. Hold a step while turning E3 for a local exception, then release it. To add a trig mask, hold K1, tap that step and release K1. Steps 1–16 are row 4, 17–32 row 5, 33–48 row 6 and 49–64 row 7. Column is the position within that group. For Song slots, press Song at (6,8); slots 1–3 are (1,1)–(3,1). Hold the source slot, tap the destination and release; then tap the destination to edit it. Set Song Tempo to 90 and each channel Rate to /1, applying changes with K3. In Trig params, E2 selects a slot, K2 opens its assignment list, E3 highlights a parameter, K3 assigns it and K2 returns. Hold a step and turn E3 to set its lock. K2 clears a held-step lock.

Relative-turn comparison — compare longer and shorter Decay tails while keeping the note pattern fixed. In Song, select slot 1 and set its length to 32 steps with no parameter locks; this is the two-bar straight reference. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and keep slot 2 at 32 steps. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. Open Channel tasks → Trig params and assign Decay to slot 1. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 clockwise by 200 detents; release it. Repeat the 200-detent turn on step 9 and release. Then hold step 5 and turn E3 clockwise by 40 detents; release it. Repeat the 40-detent turn on step 13 and release. Check: steps 1 and 9 form the longer-tail group; steps 5 and 13 form the shorter-tail group, while the note pattern stays fixed. These turns are relative to the current setting; the absolute Decay value shown depends on its starting value and your device. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1 to restore the plain line.

Separate endpoint practice — try the 0.1 s and 3.2 s endpoints. In Song set slot 1 to 32 steps with no parameter locks. Copy slot 1 to slot 2 and set its length to 32. Tap slot 2 before editing its locks. In slot 2, hold step 1 and turn E3 anticlockwise until the displayed Decay reaches its 0.1 s minimum, then clockwise to the displayed 3.2 s maximum; release the step. Repeat the 3.2 s setting on step 9. Set Decay to 0.1 s on steps 5 and 13, releasing each step afterward. Check the Trig params readout for the long settings on 1 and 9 and short settings on 5 and 13. Select slot 1 before comparing the two slots. Play slots 1 and 2, then stop and select slot 1. On your instrument, compare the tails while the notes stay in the same order.

Restore: Select slot 1 to restore the unmodified line. Stop and return to the separate course project when finished.

Starting point: channel 1 plays the drums and channel 2 is empty. Masks work as in the percussion recipe: E2 chooses the value, E3 sets it, and holding a step gives that step its own value.

1. Select channel 2 (2,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Polyperc 1 and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 2 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (2,2) to assign Pattern 2 to channel 2.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, turn E2 to Note and set MIDI 48 (C2), turn E2 to Vel and set 42, and turn E2 to Len and set ½ step.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1, 5, 9 and 13.

4. Select Note with E2, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 55 (G2), then release. Steps 1, 5 and 13 keep the default MIDI 48.

5. Listen: press Play. In bar 1, the bass plays C2 on beats 1, 2 and 4 and G2 on beat 3 under the bar-1 drums; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

6. Repeat steps 3 and 4 in bars 2 to 4, adding 16 to each step number of bar 1. Each trig list is followed by the step that takes MIDI 55:
Bar 2: trigs on 17, 21, 25, 29; 25 is MIDI 55.
Bar 3: trigs on 33, 37, 41, 45; 41 is MIDI 55.
Bar 4: trigs on 49, 53, 57, 61; 57 is MIDI 55.

Listen for the pitch pattern C, C, G, C repeating once per bar under the drums.

parsed_allowlist.before:
Starting point: channels 1 and 2 play the drums and bass; channel 3 is empty. Use Doubledecker for the chord because it plays several notes at once. On Masks and Pattern Trig, all 64 steps are visible together: row 4 is steps 1–16, row 5 is 17–32, row 6 is 33–48 and row 7 is 49–64; the column is 1 + (step−1) modulo 16. These screens do not page. Pattern Note and Velocity use 16-step pages. Hold K1 and tap to add or remove a trig; hold a step and turn E3 to give it its own value.

1. Select channel 3 (3,1). Turn E1 to Channel tasks, turn E2 to Device, press K3, turn E3 to Doubledecker and press K3 to assign it. Open Channel (3,8), select channel 3 on row 1, then tap pattern slot (3,2) to assign Pattern 3 to channel 3.

2. Open Masks. With no step held, set Note to MIDI 60 (C3), Vel to 26 and Len to 3 steps. Select Chd1 and set 3rd; select Chd2 and set 5th. Every chord now plays the root plus the notes a third and a fifth above it in the scale.

3. In bar 1, hold K1 and tap steps 1 and 9. Select Note, hold step 9 and turn E3 to MIDI 62 (D3), then release. Step 1 keeps the default MIDI 60. Press Play: in bar 1 the chord alternates C-E-G and D-F-A, two chords a bar, quietly above the bass; bars 2–4 remain silent until you enter them. Press Stop.

4. Bar 2: add trigs on steps 17 and 25.

5. Set step 25 to MIDI 62 as in step 3.

6. Bar 3: add trigs on steps 33 and 41.

7. Set step 41 to MIDI 62.

8. Bar 4: hold K1 and tap steps 49 and 57.

9. Hold step 49 and set Note to MIDI 67 (G3). Step 57 keeps the default MIDI 60.

10. Result check: listen to the whole four bars: press Play and wait for bar 4. The drums and bass repeat unchanged, but the chords move to G-B-D and then back to C-E-G. The chord intervals follow the C-major scale, so the 3rd above D is F and the 3rd above G is B. Press Stop.
